analysis:
The only change is documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 980-1027), which adds a startup shape-warmup description. The rest of the supplied text is unchanged context. I found no source code, wire, authorization, attestation, key-handling or cache-storage change to evaluate.

The documented behavior is local calibration. It runs excluded probes and cells and trains no rates or counters. It uses a 20-second wall budget and runs after self-test and before registration. Warmup prompts are synthetic provider-generated prompts, not consumer data (A-001). The text does not state whether they are cache-scoped, so the prefix-cache interaction (T-041) is unverified. I did not verify that warmup donations are excluded from the SSD prefix cache or scoped away from consumer cacheSalt values. The documented behavior does not plainly weaken T-041, and the claim in the doc is not contradicted by the supplied evidence.

The warmup could affect availability (T-029, T-057-style startup delay), but the doc bounds it with the 20-second budget, the registration gate's timeout, preemption by customer requests and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0 rollback.

Docs-only claims about cold-cache timing cannot be validated here. ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift and EngineV2Bridge+ShapeWarmup.swift were not supplied, so the implementation matches the doc only on trust. A reviewer should confirm that warmup requests never publish to the SSD prefix cache or to resident checkpoints, and never feed capacity or routing evidence. No threat model update is needed from a doc-only change.
